memory_update.text: CRDO should be tracked as a direct AI networking interconnect candidate because its optical DSPs, AECs, and Microsoft HiWire Switch AEC relationship map to rack/ToR and transceiver connectivity.

COHR and LITE are direct optical-component candidates for 800G/1.6T AI networking; key differentiators to verify are InP/EML capacity, silicon photonics transition risk, and customer qualification depth.
FN is a second-order optical manufacturing capacity candidate; AI linkage is less direct and requires customer and product mix verification.
KEYS maps to the validation chokepoint: 1.6T Ethernet, optical/copper interconnects, 224G lanes, and AI data-center network emulation may become gating items before mass deployment.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around AI data-center networking beyond the obvious Ethernet switch and ASIC leaders. The strongest second-order mappings found in this pass are optical/component suppliers, active electrical cable and DSP silicon, optical manufacturing services, and validation/test infrastructure for 800G/1.6T Ethernet and optical interconnect.
